title: Hence from My Soul, Sad Thoughts, Be Gone
description: Hence from My Soul, Sad Thoughts, Be Gone in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 73, headed “Doubts scattered; or, Spiritual joy restored”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hence from my soul, sad thoughts, be gone, And leave me to my joys, My tongue shall tri-umph in my God, And make a joy-ful noise.

lines: Hence from my soul, sad thoughts, be gone,
And leave me to my joys,
My tongue shall triumph in my God,
Darkness and doubts had veil'd my mind,
And drown'd my head in tears,
Till sovereign grace with shining rays
O what immortal joys I felt,
When Jesus told me, I was his,
In vain the tempter frights my soul,
And breaks my peace in vain,
One glimpse, dear Saviour, of thy face,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
